caption: The drawing depicts a single metallic door knocker centered on a plain, light beige background. The knocker is vertically oriented and features ornate details. The top mounting plate is an irregular, symmetrical, decorative shape with two small round holes for screws or bolts, and two curled, scroll-like projections at the upper corners. Attached to this backplate is a round, slightly domed pivot point from which the handle extends downward in a gentle curve. The handle is mainly straight with a turned, ribbed section in the middle, suggesting a period style. The lower end of the handle is attached to a smaller, similarly shaped mounting plate that also has two round holes for fastening. The entire knocker is rendered in shades of brown with a weathered, rusted appearance, showing shadow and highlights that suggest metallic texture and aging. The composition is simple and centered, with no other objects present.
title: Suffolk Latch
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
